newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian opposition backs labour law transfer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian opposition backs labour law transfer.

text.p: The Australian opposition and the minor Australian Democrats party said on Monday they endorsed the state of Victoria's plan to hand over its industrial relations powers to the federal government.
Opposition industrial relations spokesman Bob McMullan said he supported the referral if it simplified the system
"... if the referral of the powers (to the federal government) will truly reduce the complexity of administering industrial law in Victoria, it must be a good thing," he said.
But he cautioned that he needed more time to study the details of the proposal before giving a full response.

Australian Democrats leader Cheryl Kernot said the referral would help both workers and employers by removing duplication and retain the Victorian workers access to the national rules regulating unfair dismissals.

"I will be seeking assurances from both governments that the transfer of the unfair dismissals jurisdiction will occur as soon as possible to ensure that there is no hiatus between the current system and the new one," Kernot said in a statement.
She said she would give her provisional support to the early passage of national legislation.

Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said the referral of powers would benefit the Victorian workforce and boost business efficiency, notably without wasteful state and national jurisdictional contests.
"It will mean Victorian employers and employees will not have to face the administrative and legalistic hurdles normally associated with movement in the federal system," Reith said in a statement.
